name: jadeite
//description: This becomes the .desktop Comment= and the deb's extended description. Per the freedesktop spec a Comment must not restate Name (JADEITE) or GenericName (Economy Journal), so this says what the application does rather than what it is called; the name pair lives in electron-builder.yml's synopsis and GenericName. Keep it under about 78 characters — fpm and deb.erb each prepend a space, and two leading spaces make the line verbatim, so a longer one will not reflow in apt show. No apostrophes: smarten() rewrites them into curly quotes.
description: Keeps income, expenses, payments and valuables in one encrypted file
//homepage: The address the packages carry (pacman's `url`, the deb's `Homepage:`) and the one the Hakkında page prints, from one place. Until Realisation X it was in two, and neither was here: the About page held a string literal, and electron-builder derived the package field from `.git/config`'s origin remote — untracked, so the value depended on how the machine had cloned. A git worktree has no `.git/config` at all (`.git` is a file there), and `getGitUrlFromGitConfig` reads it as a directory, so fpm aborted with `Please specify project homepage`. A source tarball, which is how an AUR build works, has no `.git` either. Committed here, the address is a fact of the project rather than of the clone.
//desktopName: Must equal the app_id the running window reports, which is app.setName('jadeite') in src/main/index.ts. electron-builder writes StartupWMClass from this; without it the key falls back to productName and the entry claims a class of JADEITE that no window ever has, so a taskbar cannot match the window to the launcher icon.

scripts.audit: node scripts/audit-colours.mjs && node scripts/audit-locale.mjs && node scripts/audit-egress.mjs && node scripts/audit-strings.mjs
scripts.typecheck: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.e2e.json
scripts.test: npm run audit && vitest run && npm run test:vault
scripts.//package:win: Built on Windows, never cross-packed from Linux — see the asarUnpack comment in electron-builder.yml. node-gyp-build prefers build/Release over prebuilds, so a Linux tree packed for Windows ships an ELF argon2.node that fails at first unlock. npmRebuild is turned off here and only here: on Windows both native modules already hold the right binary for Electron's ABI before packaging starts — argon2 through its win32-x64 prebuild, which is N-API and therefore ABI-stable across Node and Electron alike, and better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers through the published electron-v146 prebuild that `prebuild-install --runtime=electron --target=42.8.0` fetches. Left on, @electron/rebuild does not recognise prebuildify's layout, falls through to node-gyp for argon2, and demands a Visual Studio installation in order to rebuild something that did not need rebuilding. Linux keeps the rebuild and genuinely needs it: better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers is not N-API, so npm installs its Node-ABI prebuild there and only the rebuild makes the packaged application openable.
scripts.//package:dir: Kept deliberately though nothing calls it: `verify:package` runs the full `package` so tests/package/metadata.spec.ts has a .pacman and a .deb to read. This is the fast path for iterating on the packaged suite itself — it produces release/linux-unpacked, which is everything packaged.spec.ts needs, without paying fpm for both targets. Global rule 7 is about code that runs once and is carried forever; this runs whenever somebody edits that suite.
scripts.verify:package: npm run package && playwright test -c playwright.package.config.ts
scripts.//verify:package:win: The Windows counterpart, and it must exist separately because `package` hard-codes --linux: an npm script cannot branch on platform, and a Windows machine asked to run verify:package would build a pacman and a deb it cannot make. The suite behind both is the same one. packaged.spec.ts resolves release/win-unpacked rather than release/linux-unpacked; metadata.spec.ts skips itself here, because the .pacman and .deb members it reads are not among the things --win produces.
scripts.verify:package:win: npm run package:win && playwright test -c playwright.package.config.ts
